name: ide_history
description: Read IDE local history (VSCode Timeline history and JetBrains Local History) for a file that is not recoverable from git. Use action=list to find historical versions of a path and action=read with the entry timestamp to fetch the content. Read-only.

path.description: Absolute file path to filter by (list/read).

timestamp.description: Entry timestamp in epoch milliseconds, from a list result (read).

name: exit_plan_mode
description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

name: ask_user_question
description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding. Send one or more questions, each with a stable id that will be echoed in the answer.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

name: bash
description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. On Windows this bash is Git-Bash (MSYS2), not WSL: drives appear as `/c/...`, Windows executables run directly, and Linux-only tools are missing — use the `wsl` tool for a real Linux distribution. For PowerShell use `pwsh` (PowerShell 7, cross-platform) or, on Windows only, `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1). Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Background execution is not available; long-running commands must finish within the timeout.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session working directory; a relative path is resolved against it.

envs.description: Environment variables to set for this command (object of string values). `DSH_*` keys are ignored.

name: bash_persistent
description: Run commands in a persistent bash shell. State, including the current directory and exported environment variables, persists across calls for this agent. On Windows this bash is Git-Bash (MSYS2), not WSL; use `pwsh_persistent` for a persistent PowerShell session.

command.description: The bash command to run. Relative path is preferred in the command.

name: board_post
description: Post a message to this delegation tree's shared board. Peer coordination only: material findings, questions, blockers, candidate results. The full formatted message must fit within 4 KiB.

to.description: Recipient: a participant session id, "main" (the root session), or "ALL".

reply_to.description: Board message id this post corrects or answers.

name: board_read
description: Read this delegation tree's shared board incrementally. Pass the cursor from your last read as `since`; the result carries the next cursor, a hasMore flag, and the participant roster.

since.description: Cursor from your last board_read; omit to read from the beginning.

name: board_claim
description: Soft-reserve a file region (advisory line lock) before editing it. Overlapping claims come back as conflicts; the claim auto-expires after ttl seconds if you forget to release it.

name: board_release
description: Release your soft-reserved file region claim(s): pass claim_id, or path to release all your claims on that path.

name: read
description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

name: read_image
description: Read a local image file (PNG/JPEG/GIF/BMP/PBM/TGA/TIFF/WEBP/EXR/QOI/ICO/CUR/ANI) and return the image itself to the model. Images whose long edge exceeds 2000px are downscaled automatically; the result states the original size and the coordinate multiplier.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved like the read tool (relative paths use the session working directory). Extension-less files are identified by their content.

name: write
description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

name: edit
description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

name: glob
description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session working directory; a relative path resolves against it.

name: grep
description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session working directory; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

name: get_goal
description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

name: create_goal
description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

name: update_goal
description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

name: job_output
description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

name: job_list
description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

name: job_kill
description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

name: present
description: Declare existing files as final deliverables for the user. Use it when the user needs a separate file, especially Office documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks; prefer your final response when that suffices. The user opens the current files; their contents are not copied.

files.description: Usually the 1-2 most important deliverables; at most 8 per call.

path.description: Path of an existing regular file. Relative paths resolve against the session working directory.

name: pwsh
description: Execute a PowerShell 7 command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use the host's native form (`C:\...` on Windows); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. pwsh is cross-platform PowerShell 7; on Windows prefer it over `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1) unless a command needs 5.1-only modules or COM. On Linux/macOS native commands and paths are case-sensitive, and `ls`/`cat`/`curl` are the real executables rather than aliases. Use `bash` for POSIX shell syntax and `wsl` for a Linux distribution on Windows. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$env:DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Background execution is not available; long-running commands must finish within the timeout.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session working directory; a relative path is resolved against it.

envs.description: Environment variables to set for this command (object of string values). `DSH_*` keys are ignored.

name: pwsh_persistent
description: Run PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`) commands in a persistent session. State, including the current location, variables, functions, imported modules and `$env:` changes, persists across calls for this agent. All output streams are merged into one text result. A failed command ends with `[exit code: N]`: N is the exit code of the last native command when it failed, otherwise 1 when the last statement reported an error or a terminating error was thrown. `exit` ends the session and the next call starts a fresh one. Use `pwsh` for a one-off command, `bash_persistent` for persistent POSIX shell state, and `powershell` (Windows only) when Windows PowerShell 5.1 is required.

command.description: The PowerShell command to run. Relative path is preferred in the command.

name: schedule_create
description: Create a reminder in the current session that delivers prompt back to this session when it becomes due. Supply exactly one timing parameter: after_seconds, at, every_seconds, daily, weekly, or cron. Local times that do not exist in the zone are skipped; repeated local times fire once, at the earlier instant. When the session is resumed after being closed, an overdue one-shot is delivered once and a recurring reminder delivers only its latest missed occurrence.

prompt.description: Reminder content to deliver when the target becomes due.

title.description: Concise task name in the user's language, at most 120 characters. Name only the core action and subject; keep essential target identifiers such as PR numbers and branch names. Do not include execution frequency, scheduled dates or times, time zones, task status, or execution details. Put scheduling information in the timing parameters and execution instructions in prompt.

every_seconds.description: Fixed-rate interval in whole seconds, at least 60, aligned to the time it is saved.

daily.description: Every day at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 23:00:00.125.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekly.description: On the given weekdays at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 09:00:00.125.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekdays.description: ISO weekdays, Monday 1 through Sunday 7, without repetitions.

cron.description: Five-field Vixie cron expression in a time zone.

expression.description: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, for example "*/15 9-17 * * 1-5". Numeric values, *, ascending ranges, */n, a-b/n, and comma-separated lists only; no names, macros, ?, L, W, #, or seconds field. If either day field starts with *, both day fields must match; otherwise either may match.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

at.description: Absolute one-shot target: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits and uppercase Z or a numeric offset +/-HH:mm (00-23 hours, 00-59 minutes; not -00:00), or a local date, time, and time_zone. A local time that does not exist in the zone is rejected; a repeated local time uses the earlier instant.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

name: schedule_list
description: List the active reminders in the current session.

name: schedule_update
description: Change a reminder in place, keeping its id. Supply a new title, prompt, or at most one timing parameter; omitted fields keep their stored values. To change a relative delay, create a new reminder.

title.description: New task name; follow the schedule_create title rules.

every_seconds.description: Fixed-rate interval in whole seconds, at least 60, aligned to the time it is saved.

daily.description: Every day at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 23:00:00.125.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekly.description: On the given weekdays at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 09:00:00.125.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekdays.description: ISO weekdays, Monday 1 through Sunday 7, without repetitions.

cron.description: Five-field Vixie cron expression in a time zone.

expression.description: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, for example "*/15 9-17 * * 1-5". Numeric values, *, ascending ranges, */n, a-b/n, and comma-separated lists only; no names, macros, ?, L, W, #, or seconds field. If either day field starts with *, both day fields must match; otherwise either may match.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

at.description: Absolute one-shot target: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits and uppercase Z or a numeric offset +/-HH:mm (00-23 hours, 00-59 minutes; not -00:00), or a local date, time, and time_zone. A local time that does not exist in the zone is rejected; a repeated local time uses the earlier instant.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

name: schedule_delete
description: Delete a reminder in the current session, active or ended. Deletion does not retract a reminder message that is already queued.

name: session_search
description: Search earlier conversation history for a keyword and return matching sessions with snippets.

query.description: Keywords to search for in user, assistant and tool text.

name: str_replace_editor
description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* A null placeholder for a parameter unused by the selected command is treated as omitted. Required parameters still need values; omit `str_replace.new_str` rather than setting it to null when deleting a match

Notes for using the `str_replace` command:
* The `old_str` parameter should match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the original file. Be mindful of whitespaces!
* If the `old_str` parameter is not unique in the file, the replacement will not be performed. Make sure to include enough context in `old_str` to make it unique
* The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that should replace the `old_str`

command.description: The commands to run. Allowed options are: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory, e.g. `/repo/file.py` or `/repo`.

file_text.description: Required string parameter of `create` command, with the content of the file to be created. A null placeholder is treated as omitted by commands that do not use this parameter.

insert_line.description: Required integer parameter of `insert` command. The `new_str` will be inserted AFTER the line `insert_line` of `path`. A null placeholder is treated as omitted by commands that do not use this parameter.

new_str.description: Optional string parameter of `str_replace` command containing the new string (if omitted, no string will be added). Required string parameter of `insert` command containing the string to insert. A null placeholder is accepted only by commands that do not use this parameter.

old_str.description: Required string parameter of `str_replace` command containing the string in `path` to replace. A null placeholder is treated as omitted by commands that do not use this parameter.

view_range.description: Optional parameter of `view` command when `path` points to a file. If omitted or null, the full file is shown. If provided, the file will be shown in the indicated line number range, e.g. [11, 12] will show lines 11 and 12. Indexing at 1 to start. Setting `[start_line, -1]` shows all lines from `start_line` to the end of the file.

name: subagent
description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. Set `run_in_background: true` to get a job id back immediately instead of waiting for the result. Child LLM selection is optional: omit `provider`, `model` and `reasoning_effort` to use the configured child defaults and inherit the rest from this conversation. To run the child on another route, call `list_subagent_models` and pass one listed `provider` and `model` together; changing the route without `reasoning_effort` uses that model's default effort.

description.description: A short (3–5 word) description of the task to delegate.

prompt.description: The prompt for the subagent. The subagent does not have any of your conversation history, so include all necessary information and context in the prompt.

run_in_background.description: Set to `true` to run this subagent in the background. `true` returns a background job id immediately; `false` waits and returns the subagent's final reply.

provider.description: LLM provider id for the child, as listed by `list_subagent_models`. Supply together with `model`; omit both to keep the default route.

model.description: Model id for the child, as listed by `list_subagent_models` for that provider. Supply together with `provider`.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort for the child's route, one of the efforts `list_subagent_models` lists for it. Omit to inherit a compatible effort or use a newly selected model's default.

name: send_message
description: Send a message to a live direct child subagent; the target treats it as a user message injected at the next step boundary. Also usable toward the direct parent of this session while running as a subagent.

content.description: Plain-text content delivered as one user message.

target.description: Address a direct child subagent, or the direct parent while running as a subagent.

childId.description: Target child subagent id (from `subagent` with run_in_background, or `list_agents`). Required when target is `child`.

name: interrupt_agent
description: Interrupt a live direct child subagent (cancels its current work). Unknown or already-finished ids are accepted as a no-op.

childId.description: Child subagent id to interrupt (from `subagent` with run_in_background, or `list_agents`).

name: list_agents
description: List the durable subagent identity of every session-backed subagent of this session (continuable and one-shot). Use `scope: "children"` for direct children or `scope: "descendants"` for the whole subtree. Corrupt rows are kept as diagnostic entries.

scope.description: Enumeration scope: `children` lists direct children, `descendants` lists the entire subtree.

name: list_subagent_models
description: List the LLM routes available to subagents without changing the current agent. Each row is one provider and model (with its reasoning efforts when advertised) that can be passed unchanged as the subagent tool's `provider`, `model` and `reasoning_effort`. Only providers with a configured API key are listed. Pass `provider` to list a single provider's models.

provider.description: Registered LLM provider id. Omit to list the routes of every provider.

name: terminal_open
description: Create a persistent, owner-isolated terminal session from a registered backend type. Use this for shell or REPL state that must survive across tool calls.

name.description: Optional owner-local display name such as "main" or "gdb".

cwd.description: Initial working directory. Defaults to the session working directory; a relative path resolves against it.

name: terminal_send
description: Send text to a persistent terminal. By default Enter is submitted and the call waits for a prompt, stdin wait, output silence, timeout, or session exit. Background mode returns a job id for job_output/job_kill.

sessionId.description: Terminal session id returned by terminal_open or terminal_list.

text.description: UTF-8 text to write to the terminal.

submit.description: Submit Enter after text (default true). Set false for control characters or incomplete REPL input.

run_in_background.description: Return a job id immediately; collect with job_output or stop with job_kill.

name: terminal_read
description: Read a bounded page of retained output from a persistent terminal without sending input.

count.description: Requested line count (default 500; backend caps apply).

name: terminal_signal
description: Send an allowed signal to the current foreground process group of a persistent terminal.

signal.description: Signal to deliver. Shell-targeted SIGKILL is rejected; use terminal_close.

name: terminal_close
description: Close one persistent terminal and wait until its captured owned process tree is gone.

name: terminal_list
description: List persistent terminal sessions owned by the current agent.

name: todo_write
description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

name: working_directory
description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths in file tools and newly started shells and terminals resolve against it. Existing persistent shells and terminals keep their own directories. The write permission root stays at the session's original directory: writing outside it, or starting a shell outside it, needs user approval.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter, absolute or relative to the current directory. Omit to read the current directory.

name: create_worktree
description: Create a new Git branch and worktree from a local commit, branch, or tag, then change this session's working directory to it. The checkout goes to <current checkout root>/.agents/worktrees/<name>. Defaults to HEAD and a generated name; no fetch is performed. Uncommitted files stay in the source checkout. Existing branch names or checkout paths fail. Use working_directory with cd to leave; the checkout and branch remain.

name.description: New branch name, also used as the checkout directory. Omit to generate a unique name.

from.description: Local commit, branch, or tag to start from. Defaults to HEAD.

name: web_search
description: Search the web for current information. Provide 1–4 queries in the required queries array; set engine to search a specific source such as GitHub or Stack Overflow (the system prompt lists the usable engines). Returns an optional summary answer, a list of source URLs, and the answering engine with its limitations.

queries.description: Required search queries; accepts 1–4 items and merges their results.

engine.description: Optional search engine id applied to every query, for example baidu, google, bing, duckduckgo, github-repos, github-code or stackoverflow; omit it for the default general web search.

name: web_fetch
description: Fetch the content of a specific HTTP(S) URL and return it decoded to text.

name: ralph
description: Run a foreground fresh-agent Ralph loop toward one immutable objective. Use only when the direct human explicitly asks for Ralph or fresh-agent iteration. Each round opens a new child with no parent conversation or prior child session; the shared workspace is long-term memory, and only a bounded structured report crosses rounds. The call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or at the round limit. Ordinary long-running same-session work belongs to goal tools.

objective.description: The immutable completion objective for every fresh Ralph round.

maxRounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer round cap, bounded by the deployment ceiling.

name: workflow
description:
Run a C# workflow program that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a program instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the C# statement body ONLY (plain statements run inside an async method — NOT a class or method declaration), executed on the same C# script host as run_code: `await` is available and `return <JsonNode?>` ends the program. Build the result from `JsonNode`/`JsonObject`/`JsonArray`/`JsonValue`; return `null` for nothing. Because a `JsonNode` can have only one parent, call `.DeepClone()` before placing a value into a second structure (agent() results are already detached).

Program-body helpers:
- `await agent(string prompt, JsonObject? opts = null): Task<JsonNode?>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts["schema"]` it resolves to the child's final text (a string `JsonValue`); with `opts["schema"]` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails. Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `await pipeline(JsonArray items, params Func<JsonNode?, JsonNode?, int, Task<JsonNode?>>[] stages): Task<JsonNode?>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage is an `async (prev, item, index) => ...` lambda. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `await parallel(Func<Task<JsonNode?>>[] thunks): Task<JsonNode?>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `await phase(string title)` — start a progress phase; `await log(string message)` — narrate progress; `JsonNode? args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused helpers (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the program — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply, and the program runs in a separate C# process. Let the agents do the work — use `agent(...)` for anything that must go through the audited subagent pipeline — and keep the script to coordination. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole program finishes.

script.description: The C# workflow program statement body (runs inside an async method: `await` allowed; end with `return <JsonNode?>`; plain statements only, no class/method declaration).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).
